[IMPORTANT: Results were written using a randomized dataset produced by Qualtrics to simulate what these sections will look like after data collection. These will be updated following the data collection.]
Action identification refers to the observer's interpretation of an actor's action, whereas mind attribution refers to the extent to which the observer acknowledges the existence of mental states in the actor's behaviour (Kozak et al, 2006). The level of action identification toward an actor could associate with the extent of mind attribution on him. In a pre-registered experiment with randomized dataset produced by Qualtrics (N = 65), we conducted a replication of Study 1, 2, 3, and 5 of Kozak et al. (2006).
decisions.location: Abstract, lines 131-132 (see also Method, line 245, and Results, line 520)
decisions.reason: The primary source confirms the target identity (Studies 1, 2, 3, and 5 of Kozak, Marsh, & Wegner, 2006, 10.1037/0022-3514.90.4.543) and replication design, but explicitly states in the Abstract, Method, and Results headers that all reported results were generated from a randomized dataset produced by Qualtrics to simulate what the sections will look like after data collection, with blank Discussion and Conclusion sections. The shipped outcome ('mixed') and quote reflect a later completed manuscript not present in this pre-registration source text. Because only simulated placeholder statistics are present in the supplied primary text, the empirical replication outcome is undeterminable (consistent with the blind coding of 'cannot_be_determined' for prospective simulated data).
